source.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka SAEs

page_placements.theme: SAE width, sparsity, architecture, regularizers and supervision change latent monosemanticity

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on SAE latents, not on whether individual neurons in the underlying language model are polysemantic.
record.gate_note: The reported absorption, splitting, composition, probing, and interpretability results concern SAE latents. They do not measure neuron polysemanticity or test any listed version. SAE-level findings are recorded under fits_no_version; cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The post trains Matryoshka and BatchTopK SAEs on Gemma-2-2B residual stream and evaluates SAE latents (absorption, splitting, composition, probing, autointerp). It measures no model neurons and does not test whether neurons are polysemantic or why. Polysemanticity is only background motivation for SAEs ('better monosemantic representations').
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude Matryoshka SAEs trade worse reconstruction for much lower absorption, splitting and composition and better concept isolation, with similar CE loss; probing and autointerp results are mixed, and the approach is promising but needs more validation.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies a new SAE training architecture, not the neuron-response methods or measurements in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported SAE outcomes vary with dictionary size and nested-latent group: absorption remains low in Matryoshka SAEs as size grows, spurious-correlation removal improves with size, and interpretability differs between early and later groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Matryoshka SAEs show first-letter absorption around 0.03 vs about 0.29 for larger BatchTopK SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matryoshka SAE training reduces absorption of hierarchical features into SAE latents.

fits_no_version.finding: First-letter features nearly unified in Matryoshka SAEs but often split in BatchTopK SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matryoshka SAE training reduces feature splitting across SAE latents.

fits_no_version.finding: Meta-SAEs explain substantially more variance of BatchTopK decoder directions than Matryoshka ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matryoshka SAE latents share less information (less feature composition).

fits_no_version.finding: Matryoshka SAEs outperform on TPP; SCR improves with Matryoshka size; k-sparse probing mixed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matryoshka SAE architecture improves SAE concept isolation benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Autointerp scores 0.84-0.88 across all; early Matryoshka groups slightly higher, later slightly lower, possibly noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated interpretability of Matryoshka SAE latents differs across nested groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Matryoshka SAEs reconstruct worse (MSE, variance explained) but have similar downstream CE loss at largest sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matryoshka regularization costs reconstruction more than downstream loss.

record.problems: Only one Matryoshka SAE was trained. Many comparisons are reported qualitatively without exact metric values or uncertainty estimates. Automated interpretability differences are described as subtle and possibly noise; the authors note that human-judge interpretability remains to be investigated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant SAE-level outcomes were omitted.

untested.parts: No transformer MLP neurons measured; only residual-stream SAE latents.
Superposition as cause of neuron polysemanticity not tested; sparsity effects discussed only for SAE latents.
No neuron polysemanticity from initialization, regularization or noise measured.
Architecture comparison concerns SAEs, not the share of polysemantic neurons in the model.
Autointerp scoring applied to SAE latents only; no neuron-level measurement comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the post does not discuss neuron polysemanticity versions, only mentions monosemanticity as a goal of SAEs. All rows concern SAE latents and correctly carry versions ['none']; their cannot_determine states are fine as they bear on no version. Only one Matryoshka SAE trained; most comparisons given without numbers.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier neurons or InceptionV1 neurons are studied.
No transformer MLP neurons or neuron responses to tokens or contexts are measured.
The post discusses feature absorption and sparsity in SAEs but does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by representing more features than neurons.
No neuron polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise is measured.
The comparison concerns SAE architectures and SAE-latent properties, not the share of polysemantic neurons or a neuron-level performance trade-off.
No canonical polysemantic neurons are reinterpreted as detectors of a shared feature.
No neuron-polysemanticity measure is compared across activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

relation.reason: The post only touches the topic in passing. It cites Bills et al.'s neuron-explainer as the basis for its autointerp method and closes by hoping for 'better monosemantic representations'. It never discusses polysemantic neurons, so 'discusses' would overstate the contact and cites_only fits best.

tranche.reason: The post studies SAE training and measures SAE latents, not neurons, so it neither tests nor uses the claim.

source_check.notes: Row r3 is about SAE latent absorption: the study's own method (Matryoshka) compared with BatchTopK on Gemma-2-2B layer 8. It is not about neuron polysemanticity, so versions=none and cannot_determine are right. It serves only as an example of why the study does not fit. The text never uses the word polysemantic.

statements.problem: none; the text gives about 0.03 for Matryoshka and about 0.29 for the larger BatchTopK SAEs, both on the first-letter absorption task
